# Agent instructions: dotnet-agent-kit

This repo is **dotnet-agent-kit**, a versioned engineering method for .NET repos and coding agents. It holds rules with sources and enforcement, checks, agent instructions and templates. The kit applies its own rules here.

## Whose rules win

1. **Floor:** legal, safety, security, privacy and license compliance. Never overridden.
2. **Owner:** what the owner (Derek) stated or ratified, including accepted ADRs.
3. **Outside authorities:** Microsoft Learn, the Azure Well-Architected Framework, OWASP and similar. The more specific source wins; a real conflict goes to an ADR.

Anything an agent suggests is **proposed** until the owner accepts it. Rules marked `status: proposed` in `docs/standards/` aren't in force.

## Working modes

Agents work in one of two modes (ADR-0035). At the start of each task, check which. Read `.agent-mode` at the repo root: it's **auto** unless that file says `review`. `Set-AgentMode.ps1` with no `-Mode` also prints the mode, without a prompt (`./tools/` in the kit, `./.kit/tools/` with `-RepoRoot .` in an app). The file is gitignored, so each person's mode is their own, and each checkout's: a new worktree starts in auto. Switching is the owner's call: Claude Code asks before any run with `-Mode`, and other agents follow this rule.

- **Auto, the default.** Work through the agreed roadmap without waiting for approval: post the plan in chat, then build it. You may add a dependency that the kit's standards or ADRs, or the official docs they cite, name for the task; say so in the PR. Merge your own PR with a merge commit (`gh pr merge <n> --merge`) once CI has passed at its head commit, the latest `reviewer` round on that commit has no unanswered blocking or should-fix finding (or on the commit before the final round's nit fixes, when those change no behavior and are listed in its PR comment; `finish-work` steps 2 and 5), and the description is complete (for a PR whose description a bot writes, DOD-006's comment at that commit). Then report what merged. You may merge a Dependabot PR the same way when it's only a patch or minor update of NuGet packages, .NET tools or the .NET SDK; a major update, any update of a 0.x package, or a GitHub Actions bump is the owner's to merge (ADR-0041). Decide a "won't fix" yourself, with the reason in the reply. "Always ask" still applies, and so does one exception: a PR that changes the guardrails themselves needs the owner's yes for that PR. Ask him in the chat, naming the head commit, once its final review round is clean and CI has passed; on his yes, merge it yourself at that commit. A commit pushed after his yes needs a new yes (owner, 2026-11-10). That means:
  - the "Working modes" or "Always ask" sections, or SEC-003;
  - `.claude/settings.json` or the `Set-AgentMode.ps1` script;
  - the `finish-work` skill or the `reviewer` agent, which enforce these rules;
  - a ruleset, branch protection or the merge settings;
  - a CI check, if removed or weakened;
  - the Dependabot cooldown in `.github/dependabot.yml` (in the kit, the app template's too), if shortened or narrowed;
  - `New-KitApp`'s step that turns on Dependabot alerts and security updates, if removed or weakened.
- **Review.** The owner approves non-trivial plans before work starts, decides each "won't fix", and merges each PR, or says to for that PR. "Also ask in review mode" applies too.

**Release PRs are never merged by an agent, in either mode.** Those are release-please's PRs, on a `release-please--` branch: releases are the owner's (owner, 2026-11-07).

## How to work

Each task runs through these steps, in order. The skills in `.claude/skills/` walk through them; their names are in brackets.

1. **Plan** (`start-work`, `plan-checklist`). State the goal, approach, files touched, and a **test list** (the behaviors to cover). Cover the five Well-Architected pillars: reliability; security, with a short threat model for anything touching data or sign-in; cost; operational excellence, including observability; performance. Add accessibility, data, and docs/ADRs. In review mode, the owner approves non-trivial plans before work starts; in auto mode, post the plan and go on.
2. **Red** (`tdd-cycle`). Turn one item from the test list into a failing test. It must fail on an assertion, not on a crash or a missing type. Commit it.
3. **Green.** Make the full suite pass. Commit.
4. **Refactor** on green, then repeat from step 2 until the list is empty. Never convert the whole list into tests up front.
5. **Decide** (`write-adr`). A significant technical choice gets an ADR in `docs/adr/`, made from the template, with at least two options and a recommendation.
6. **Verify and hand over** (`finish-work`). Run every check, get an independent review from the `reviewer` agent, then open the PR with the template. In auto mode, merge it once it's ready (see "Working modes").
7. **Answer the review** (`address-review`). When a review lands on the PR, from GitHub Copilot or a person, check every finding against the current code. Fix the real ones test-first and push. Reply to each thread with the evidence, and resolve it as addressed or incorrect. For a finding you'd recommend not fixing: in review mode, leave it open with your recommendation, because "won't fix" is the owner's call; in auto mode, decide it and give the reason. Do this again for each re-review.

## Talking to the owner

- Lead with one recommendation and a one-line reason. List options only when the answer depends on his personal preference.
- On first use, explain any term, tool or document he hasn't used himself, in plain words with an example. Refer to documents by path.
- When he answers a batch of questions, restate them with his answers as a table.
- Say in one line what a command does, then run it yourself. Don't hand him commands you can run.
- Describe a button or screen only after confirming it exists (current docs or a screenshot).
- Make cheap improvements now instead of deferring them.
- Ask every question that needs his answer in the chat where he works, never only in a pull request or another document. Don't merge past an unanswered question the pull request depends on.
- Report done only with evidence: commands run, counts, links. Say "not verified" wherever something wasn't.

Details and sources: `docs/standards/communication.md`.

## Git

- GitHub Flow: one short-lived branch per task, merged into `main` by a pull request **with a merge commit**. Never squash or rebase-merge.
- Commit subjects and PR titles are Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `refactor:`, `docs:` or `chore:`, with `!` for a breaking change.
- Mark a test-first commit with the trailer `TDD: red` and the commit that makes it pass with `TDD: green`. Put the trailer in the message's **final paragraph**, together with `Co-Authored-By:`:

  ```text
  test: reject empty titles

  TDD: red
  Co-Authored-By: ...
  ```

- Never push to `main`, force-push, or skip hooks. Merge a PR only as the working mode allows: in review mode, when the owner says so for that PR; never a release PR; a change to the guardrails only on the owner's yes for that PR at its head commit. GitHub's "main protection" ruleset rejects direct pushes, force-pushes and deletion of `main`, and allows merge commits only.
- Before pushing to a PR's branch or reporting on a PR, check that it's still open (`gh pr view <n> --json state`). The owner may merge on his own schedule. If it's merged, put new commits on a fresh branch and open a new PR.

## Always ask

In both modes, ask the owner first before you:
- use anything that costs money, or touch cloud resources;
- delete anything on GitHub, or work that isn't merged; force-push or rewrite history;
- create a new app repo (`New-KitApp`), or make anything public;
- merge a release PR, or publish a release;
- change a ruleset, branch protection or the repo's merge settings, turn off Dependabot alerts or security updates, or remove or weaken a CI check;
- add a connector (MCP server);
- install software on the owner's machine;
- switch the working mode, or merge a change to the guardrails (see "Working modes": on his yes for its head commit, you merge it);
- do anything else that can't be undone.

Claude Code prompts for the common forms of these (`.claude/settings.json`). The rest rests on this list.

Never read, print or store secrets. Sign-in is always the owner's step.

## Also ask in review mode

In review mode, also ask the owner first before you:
- add a dependency (a package in `Directory.Packages.props`, a PowerShell module, a GitHub Action);
- change CI or other repo settings;
- act outside this repo.

**When a permission rule or prompt blocks something legitimate, stop and tell the owner.** Don't rephrase the command, move it into a script or split it up to get past the rule (ADR-0026). The rule may be wrong, but changing it is the owner's call.

## Commands

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Check this machine's toolchain | `./tools/Initialize-DevMachine.ps1` |
| Show the working mode; switch it (the owner's call) | `./tools/Set-AgentMode.ps1`, with `-Mode Review` or `-Mode Auto` |
| All script tests (Pester 6) | `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tools/tests` |
| Every rule has a source and an enforcement | `./tools/Test-RuleSources.ps1` |
| Every rule in force has a quality area, and the scorecard's table is current; `-Update` rewrites the table after a rule or area changes | `./tools/Test-Scorecard.ps1` |
| Every ADR has its required sections | `./tools/Test-AdrSections.ps1` |
| List the solution's MAUI and desktop (UI) projects, which CI builds on Windows and macOS and the coverage gate exempts (ARC-010) | `./tools/Get-UiProject.ps1 -Solution dotnet-agent-kit.slnx` |
| Regenerate agent rule files after editing a standard or this file | `./tools/Build-AgentRules.ps1` |
| Check generated files are current | `./tools/Build-AgentRules.ps1 -Check` |
| PR title and commit subjects are Conventional Commits | `./tools/Test-ConventionalTitle.ps1 -Range origin/main..HEAD` |
| Every red commit is made green | `./tools/Test-RedGreenOrder.ps1 -Range origin/main..HEAD` |
| No deprecated NuGet packages | `./tools/Test-DeprecatedPackages.ps1 -Path dotnet-agent-kit.slnx` |
| Every C# project in the solution holds code of its own, and none keeps the class library template's empty `Class1` (ARC-009) | `./tools/Test-EmptyProjects.ps1 -Solution dotnet-agent-kit.slnx` |
| Nesting, statements per member, file length and LCOM4 within CRF-011's limits (proposed) | `./tools/Test-CodeShape.ps1 -Solution dotnet-agent-kit.slnx` |
| No duplicate code (CRF-003): in CI; locally only with Java and PMD, which are the owner's to install | CI: the "Duplicate code" step of `dotnet-ci.reusable.yml`. Locally: `./tools/Test-Duplication.ps1 -Solution dotnet-agent-kit.slnx -Pmd <PMD folder>/bin/pmd` (`pmd.bat` on Windows) |
| List a PR's open review findings; reply; resolve a thread | `Import-Module ./tools/KitReview.psm1`, then `Get-OpenFinding`, `Resolve-ReviewFinding`, `Add-ReviewReply` (see the `address-review` skill) |
| Build | `dotnet build` |
| .NET tests with coverage, then the coverage gate (TST-004) | Delete `TestResults` first (the gate merges every report it finds), then `dotnet test --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura --results-directory TestResults` and `./tools/Test-CoverageGate.ps1 -Path TestResults -Solution dotnet-agent-kit.slnx` |
| Mutation score (TST-004, ADR-0039): nightly in CI; optional locally | CI: `.github/workflows/mutation.yml`; read the `mutation-report` artifact of a failed run. Locally: `dotnet tool restore` installs the pinned Stryker (installing is the owner's call), then `dotnet tool run dotnet-stryker --config-file .config/stryker-config.json --solution dotnet-agent-kit.slnx`, and `./tools/Test-MutationReport.ps1 -Path <its mutation-report.json>` |
| Break code on purpose and see whether a test notices; it edits the file in place, so run it in a fresh clone (reviewers probe a change in theirs) | `./tools/Invoke-Mutant.ps1 -Path <file> -TestPath <Pester file> -Mutant @{ Name = '...'; Find = '<exact text>'; Replace = '<new text>' }`: each mutant is Killed, Survived, NotFound, Ambiguous or Error (the tests fail or run nothing on the unchanged file, or run nothing with the mutant), and the file is restored byte for byte |
| Move the curated .NET skills to a newer dotnet/skills commit (ADR-0042) | `./tools/Update-DotnetSkills.ps1` (upstream `main`), or `-Commit <sha>`; then read the diff and follow `docs/dotnet-skills.md`. The script tests check the copies match the pinned commit |

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs all of these on every pull request, plus a gitleaks secret scan. The "main protection" ruleset requires them to pass. Mutation testing runs nightly instead, and on every pull request that changes more than docs (and the agent files generated from them), the PR template, release files, agent or editor config, git hooks, spikes, templates or Pester tests; it isn't a required check. OpenSSF Scorecard (`.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`) runs on every push to `main` and weekly, not on pull requests.

The commit-msg hook in `.githooks/` rejects a commit whose subject isn't a Conventional Commit, because only a history rewrite can fix one later (ADR-0027). `./tools/Initialize-DevMachine.ps1` reports whether it's on for this clone. If the hook rejects a commit, fix the subject; never skip the hook.

`./tools/New-KitApp.ps1 -Name <Name> -Intake <answers.json>` creates a new app repo on GitHub (README, "Start a new app"; ADR-0033). The `new-app` skill asks the owner the intake cards and writes the answers file, which becomes the app's `docs/app-profile.md` (ADR-0058). Each new repo is the owner's call, so run it only when he names the repo, and run it with `-WhatIf` first.

Scripts target PowerShell 7.6 or later (`pwsh`), the current LTS (ADR-0040). Every script and check gets Pester tests, written first.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/standards/` | One file per topic. Rules sit in YAML front matter with `id`, `statement`, `layer`, `status`, `sources` and `enforcement` |
| `docs/adr/` | Decisions. ADR numbers match the brief's decision numbers (D8 is ADR-0008) |
| `docs/quality/scorecard.md` | What a "perfect" .NET app is, area by area; the rules that cover each area and its open gaps (ADR-0034). A new rule names its area here |
| `docs/corrections-log.md` | Every owner correction and what it became |
| `.claude/skills/` | The workflow skills, read by Claude Code, Visual Studio and VS Code. Some are curated .NET skills, copied unchanged from Microsoft's dotnet/skills at one pinned commit (`docs/dotnet-skills.md`, ADR-0042): never edit those copies, and where one disagrees with a kit rule, the kit rule wins |
| `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` | The independent reviewer |
| `tools/` | PowerShell 7 scripts, with tests in `tools/tests/` |

**Generated files, don't edit:** `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and every file in `.claude/rules/` and `.github/instructions/` whose first line says "Generated by Build-AgentRules.ps1". Change the source (`docs/standards/` or this file), run `./tools/Build-AgentRules.ps1`, and commit both. Hand-written files in those folders are left alone.

## Done means

- The build has zero warnings and every test passes.
- Every check passes: rule sources, the quality scorecard, ADR sections, and generated files current.
- Docs and ADRs are updated in the same PR.
- The `reviewer` agent has reviewed the change, and its findings are fixed or answered.
- The PR uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`, including the red→green evidence table. A PR whose description a bot writes gets DOD-006's comment instead.
